verdict.rationale: The public GitHub repository (supabase/supabase) describes the project as built from open source tools. The docs call the AI toolkit open source, Docker Compose self-hosting is documented, and community users call it open-source software, so the source is readable. However, the pack never names a license or shows that the whole product, including Studio, Auth and Realtime, is under an open license; the repo wording could refer only to the components it uses. missing for 10: an explicitly named open-source license (e.g. Apache-2.0/MIT) for the product's code, evidence covering all components' repos and licenses, independent hands-on confirmation of reading/building from source.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: We're building the features of Firebase using enterprise-grade open source tools.
Supabase provides an open source toolkit for developing AI applications using Postgres and pgvector.
Deploy Supabase within your own infrastructure using Docker Compose.
Open Source software that make row level security super convenient via Postgres and OAuth and that can handle subscription.
